title: Missing reentrancy guard on Vault.withdraw lets attacker drain WETH backing
root_cause: Vault.withdraw() transfers ETH to the caller via a low-level call before decrementing balances[msg.sender], violating checks-effects-interactions; a malicious receiver re-enters withdraw() while its recorded balance is still non-zero.
attacker_entrypoint: Vault.withdraw(uint256) called from an attacker-controlled contract with a malicious receive() hook; no privileged setup.
attacker_capabilities: call any public function from an EOA

severity_justification.worst_case: Attacker drains the full WETH balance of the vault in a single transaction.
severity_justification.realistic_case: Attacker drains the liquid (non-strategy) WETH portion, ~38% of TVL at current allocation.
severity_justification.program_table_mapping: Immunefi v2.2 — Direct theft of user funds (High/Critical row).

call_trace: Attacker.receive() -> Vault.withdraw(100e18)  // re-entry, balances not yet decremented
Vault.withdraw: second transfer succeeds, then balances[attacker] -= amount underflows-protected to 0
asset_delta: Attacker withdraws 200e18 against a recorded 100e18 deposit; net +100e18 stolen.
reproduction_steps: Observe vault.balance drops by 200e18 while attacker deposited 100e18
Assert balances[attacker] == 0 and attacker contract ETH == +100e18
false_positive_risks: If a nonReentrant modifier is added in an inherited base not shown in scope, the path would be blocked (verified absent).
invalidating_conditions: Finding is invalid if withdraw() decrements balances before the external call.

defense_analysis.why_it_fails: Vault.withdraw has no nonReentrant modifier and the inherited base does not define one; verified at contracts/Vault.sol:142.
Vault uses a push transfer via low-level call, not a pull pattern.

assumptions: Attacker has at least one legitimate deposit to seed balances[attacker].
triager_summary: Classic CEI reentrancy with a runnable PoC proving a 100e18 net theft. Permissionless, in scope, fully traced.
